title: The conditional exact kinetic-energy drop
spoken: The kinetic-energy drop, K before minus K after, equals L times gamma minus one.
explanation: Under the unchanged-offset premise the C terms cancel, so the frame-account difference becomes the exact kinetic-energy drop. This still does not identify the mass decrease at a finite speed.
assumptions: Two equal, opposite light pulses remove total positive energy L; their symmetry removes recoil in the body’s rest frame.
The two inertial descriptions refer to the same emission and the same body boundary; |v| < c.
These are authored modern teaching equations, not a transcription or printed-notation concordance.
The relation H − E = K + C uses the same unknown additive C before and after emission. This is a premise; conservation and subtraction do not prove it.

notes.title: Positive kinetic-energy drop
notes.explanation: ΔK means K₀ − K₁ in this card: before minus after. It is identified from the ledger subtraction only under the unchanged-offset premise.

notes.title: Emitted energy L
notes.explanation: Total energy of both opposite pulses, in the body’s rest frame. It is not the body’s unknown total energy.

notes.title: Modern Lorentz factor
notes.explanation: γ depends on the observer speed. In this modern teaching notation γ is the factor, not the speed ratio v/c. The transformation of the light energy is imported from relativity, not derived from these energy accounts.

notes.title: Subtract the rest-frame factor
notes.explanation: At zero relative speed γ is one. Subtracting one isolates the extra light energy in the moving account; it is not an independent mass-energy premise.

notes.title: Multiply the factors
notes.explanation: Multiply the known emitted energy by the excess of the moving-frame light factor over one.

notes.title: What this relation asserts
notes.explanation: Under the unchanged-offset premise the C terms cancel, so the frame-account difference becomes the exact kinetic-energy drop. This still does not identify the mass decrease at a finite speed.
